facts.raw_span: six months of progressive generalized weakness
a 40-pound weight loss over four months
two weeks of dyspnea
mucosal pallor and non-tender, rubbery axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy
Hemoglobin 6.6 g/dL
White blood cell count 3.5 ×10^9/L
bilateral pleural effusions
high titers of ANA, anti–double-stranded DNA, and anti–Smith antibodies
low complement C3 levels
non–anion gap metabolic acidosis with hyperkalemia
pericardial effusion
morning serum aldosterone was less than 1 ng/dL

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with mucosal pallor, lymphadenopathy, high titers of ANA, anti-double-stranded DNA, and anti-Smith antibodies, low complement C3 levels, and pericardial effusion are all consistent with SLE.

The patient's renal involvement, as evidenced by proteinuria, hematuria, and decreased estimated glomerular filtration rate, in combination with the presence of high titers of ANA and anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies, suggests lupus nephritis.

The patient's severe anemia, as indicated by a hemoglobin level of 6.6 g/dL, in combination with a low white blood cell count and the presence of lymphadenopathy, suggests autoimmune hemolytic anemia.
The patient's presentation with lymphadenopathy, pleural effusions, and pericardial effusion, in combination with the presence of high titers of ANA, suggests Sjögren's syndrome.

The patient's presentation with features of lupus, scleroderma, and rheumatoid arthritis, including mucosal pallor, lymphadenopathy, high titers of ANA, and pericardial effusion, suggests mixed connective tissue disease.

rationales.F04: Lymphadenopathy is a common feature of systemic lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F05: Severe anemia is a characteristic of autoimmune hemolytic anemia.
rationales.F08: High titers of ANA, anti-double-stranded DNA, and anti-Smith antibodies are highly specific for systemic lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F09: Low complement C3 levels are often seen in systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis.
rationales.F10: Non-anion gap metabolic acidosis with hyperkalemia can occur in lupus nephritis due to renal dysfunction.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with mucosal pallor, lymphadenopathy, high titers of ANA, anti-double-stranded DNA, and anti-Smith antibodies, low complement C3 levels, and pericardial effusion are all consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus. The development of acute inflammatory arthritis and the presence of pleural and pericardial effusions further support this diagnosis.
